tier_reason: First-party numbers from public benchmark code (tools/bench_sweep.sh driving harness/src/cli.rs cmd_bench, C built by harness/build.rs) on a named CPU (i7-14700KF, WSL2), but neither the rustc nor the C compiler version is stated and the C optimisation flags come from cc-crate defaults, so not A; no independent measurement.

corrections.baseline: libopus 1.5.2 C reference as built by the repo's own harness (harness/build.rs via the cc crate): fixed-point (FIXED_POINT=1 in harness/config.h), no DNN, x86 runtime dispatch limited to SSE/SSE2/SSE4.1 (no AVX2 sources); the Apple M1 Pro rows use upstream AArch64 NEON intrinsics. Not the stock float build most distributions ship.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust: release profile lto = "thin", codegen-units = 1, target-cpu = x86-64-v3 for x86_64 and apple-a14 for aarch64-apple-darwin (.cargo/config.toml); rustc version not stated (MSRV 1.88). C reference: compiled by harness/build.rs through the cc crate with FIXED_POINT, OPUS_HAVE_RTCD, OPUS_X86_MAY_HAVE_SSE/SSE2/SSE4_1, -msse4.1 and -ffp-contract=off; the optimisation level comes from cc-crate profile defaults and the C compiler and version are not stated (a build.rs comment mentions GCC 13). libopus 1.5.2 ships silk/x86/NSQ_del_dec_avx2.c (SILK_SOURCES_AVX2) but the harness does not compile it, and the C core is not built for x86-64-v3, so code-generation flags favour the Rust side.
corrections.claimed_speedup: Rust/C time ratio on x86-64 (i7-14700KF, WSL2), medians of 5 sweeps at --iters=30 (below 1.0 means Rust faster): encode SILK NB noise 0.97x, SILK WB noise 0.96x, Hybrid noise 0.97x, CELT sweep 0.96x, CELT sine 1.00x; decode CELT square 0.92x, SILK NB 0.95x, CELT FB mono noise 0.98x, CELT sine 0.99x, CELT sweep 1.00x; worst rows encode 1.20x (CELT square, TTS speech) and decode 1.10x (SILK WB). Means 1.06x encode and 1.01x decode, i.e. parity or slightly slower. The journal's cross-sweep standard deviations (0.02-0.32 on encode, 0.01-0.09 on decode) are as large as the sub-1.0 margins, so the 'faster' rows are within noise. Apple M1 Pro means 1.16x encode and 1.22x decode (decode up to 1.50x on SILK WB), slower on every row except SILK NB/WB encode (0.99x/1.00x).
corrections.workload: ropus-compare bench (harness/src/cli.rs cmd_bench) on ten WAV vectors (SILK NB/WB noise, Hybrid noise, CELT FB mono/stereo noise, sine, sweep, square, TTS speech, stereo music) at fixed bitrates 16-128 kb/s, complexity 10, CBR, OPUS_APPLICATION_AUDIO, 20 ms frames, codec construction outside the timed loop since commit 54fef85; decode times both decoders on the same C-encoded stream; per-vector ratio is Rust total time over C total time, median across 5 sweeps of tools/bench_sweep.sh --iters=30. The bench does not compare outputs.
corrections.license: BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE is the upstream Xiph libopus BSD text plus a 2026 copyright line for the Rust port additions; ropus/Cargo.toml declares BSD-3-Clause)
corrections.caveats: Not faster than its baseline: a Rust port of libopus (already a list baseline) at roughly parity, mean encode 1.06x and decode 1.01x slower on x86-64 and 1.16x/1.22x slower on Apple M1 Pro; the few sub-1.0 rows (3-8%) sit inside the cross-sweep spread recorded in wrk_journals/2026.05.11 - JRN - perf-recalibration.md. The C side is the harness's own fixed-point build with SSE4.1-only dispatch (libopus 1.5.2's AVX2 NSQ_del_dec source is not compiled and the C code is not built for x86-64-v3), while the Rust side is compiled for x86-64-v3, so the README's 'C dispatches to hand-tuned SSE4.1/AVX2' overstates the baseline. Compiler versions are unstated, one desktop CPU under WSL2, first-party. Output equivalence: the differential harness, the seven xiph test binaries and the 24 RFC 6716/8251 vectors check decode sample-exact against C (first-party claim); encode is byte-exact except where the float tonality analysis runs (the crate README accepts about 5% byte drift on music under an SNR gate), and the benchmark itself does not compare outputs. The crates.io README (ropus/README.md) still shows the older April table (encode 1.02x, decode 0.95x, Ryzen 9950X3D) from before the 54fef85 bench fix and says both sides dispatch to AVX2. Earlier benches timed decoder construction (8.78 MB DNN weight load) rather than steady-state decode. The repo carries CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md (AI-assisted).

notes: Port of a listed baseline that is at parity, not faster; confirmed at C with the not-faster shortcoming per the batch note. Bench code read: it is like-for-like in codec settings (same bitrate, complexity 10, CBR, same C-encoded stream for decode), but the C reference is built fixed-point with SSE4.1-only dispatch while Rust gets x86-64-v3, which if anything flatters Rust. Decode is claimed sample-exact against libopus; encode is byte-exact except a documented tier-2 drift in the analysis path.

tier_reason: First-party numbers from a public harness (tools/bench/codec-bench.ps1) against FFmpeg 8.1.2's native hevc decoder, but the four benchmark streams are not published, and the CPU model, rustc version, FFmpeg build and the exact command lines are not stated, so not A; no independent measurement found.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Single core, FFmpeg 8.1.2 native hevc decoder at -threads 1, rusty_h265 0.6.0: weighted-prediction stream 703 ms vs FFmpeg 741 ms (1.05x faster, 21/21 pairs, z = +4.58); deblocking-heavy 744 vs 675 ms (0.91x, FFmpeg 1.10x faster, 1/20); 720p 8-bit mainstream inter 447 vs 267 ms (0.60x, FFmpeg 1.67x faster); 720p 10-bit 445 vs 308 ms (0.69x, FFmpeg 1.45x faster, derived from page data). The README sums this up as 'between 1.05x FASTER and 1.67x slower than ffmpeg'. FFmpeg measured against itself: 0.992x. Release 0.6.0 is 1.024-1.158x faster than 0.5.0 (all-intra to deblocking-heavy).
corrections.workload: Single-core decode of four unpublished HEVC streams (720p 8-bit mainstream inter, the same content in 10-bit, a deblocking-heavy stream, a weighted-prediction stream) with tools/bench/codec-bench.ps1: both processes pinned to one core at High priority, FFmpeg run with -threads 1 -f null - (harness default), ABBA-alternated, 21 pairs, paired win rate with z-score, frame counts checked against ffprobe, output discarded by both arms. rusty_h265 built with the bench-alloc feature (its own rusty_alloc global allocator). Timing compares unlike scopes: rusty_h265's self-reported decode_ms covers Annex-B splitting and decoding after the whole file is read into memory, while FFmpeg's -benchmark rtime covers its whole transcode loop (demuxer and parser, decoder, null-muxer pipeline threads sharing the one pinned core).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Release profile opt-level 3, codegen-units 1, panic = abort; the default build targets portable x86-64 (SSE2) with runtime-dispatched SSE4.1/AVX2 kernels, and tools/build-v3.sh builds an optional x86-64-v3 artifact (1.066x faster); the README does not say which build produced the FFmpeg table. rustc version not stated or pinned (MSRV 1.85). FFmpeg 8.1.2 build provenance and configure flags not stated (a 242 MB ffmpeg.exe on Windows per the CHANGELOG).
corrections.hardware: Not stated; Windows host (PowerShell harness, ffmpeg.exe), one pinned core (default core 4)
corrections.stars_or_usage: 2 stars; 10 commits; crates.io 520 downloads (checked 2026-10-04); the README banner claims 561 active installs (unverified)
corrections.caveats: A marginal, mixed result: faster than FFmpeg on one of four streams by 5%, slower on the other three (1.10x, 1.45x and 1.67x). The 5% win is about the size of the measurement asymmetries: rusty_h265 reports its own internal decode time while FFmpeg's rtime includes its demuxer, parser and null-muxer pipeline threads contending for the same pinned core, and the benchmarked binary uses the project's rusty_alloc allocator, which the CHANGELOG says is worth 1.133x on this decoder and which library users do not get by default. The four streams are not in the repo, the CPU model, rustc version and FFmpeg build are unstated, and the README does not say whether the portable or x86-64-v3 build was timed. Output equivalence with FFmpeg on the benchmark streams is not checked (the harness only compares frame counts); correctness rests on 147/147 JCT-VC HEVC_v1 conformance streams matched by MD5 against the reference output and per-picture SEI hashes (first-party). The README says its earlier 0.5.0 numbers did not reproduce on re-measurement, and earlier harness versions had timing bugs (15.625 ms tick accounting, process start-up charged to FFmpeg, a system-allocator reference arm). Single-threaded only, Main/Main 10 4:2:0, no Range Extensions. Rust, not C++. The HEVC decoder component of remade_ffmpeg_rs (listed for MP3/AAC/Vorbis numbers only). README opens with an install-count banner and an advert.

notes: Confirmed at C as a flagged, marginal partial win, per the batch note. Harness read in full: FFmpeg gets -threads 1 and the same pinned core, which is fair on threading, but the two timers cover different scopes and the reference stream set is unpublished, so the 1.05x is within plausible measurement bias. Not a duplicate of remade_ffmpeg_rs because that entry carries no HEVC numbers; the orchestrator may still want to cross-reference the two.
